meta.description: Download raw sequencing reads from NCBI SRA using sra-tools (prefetch, fasterq-dump, vdb-validate) or the ENA mirror. Use when pulling FASTQ for SRR/ERR/DRR accessions, deciding between SRA-direct, ENA mirror, or AWS/GCP cloud mirror (STRIDES), handling --include-technical for 10x and other single-cell records, validating with MD5/vdb-validate, navigating SRR/SRX/SRS/SRP/PRJNA hierarchy, or finding accessions via pysradb. Encodes SRA cloud-egress economics, the fasterq-dump uncompressed-scratch trap, and the --max-size default that silently truncates large prefetches.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOIs/PMIDs/p-values/sample sizes in any of the 7 outputs; the Skill only moves real, verifiable sequencing data. Unchanged from the prior re-audit.

practice_boundaries.detail: No diagnostic or prescriptive medical conclusions anywhere in this session's outputs. Unchanged from the prior re-audit.

methodological_ground.detail: The 'Controlled-access (dbGaP) data' section remains accurate and present (confirmed by direct reading of the shipped SKILL.md at commit 086e443). This round's fix additionally makes the section's own documented recognition signal (an ENA response omitting fastq_ftp) something the shipped code now actually surfaces, closing the second P1 from the pre-fix report -- verified by direct execution (Inputs 3, 4, 5, 6, 7).

code_usability.detail: The first P1 (false-positive 'md5 OK' with zero files; whole-batch abort on one bad accession) is fixed and verified far beyond the fixer's own test: this re-audit independently confirmed the guard on a synthetic fixture built from a different real accession than the fixer used, in a mixed batch at all three list positions (first/middle/last), on a reverse-column-omission case, and on a fully empty/malformed response -- 7/7 inputs executed, all behaving correctly, zero new P0/P1 found.

functional_suitability.note: Up from 10/12. Correctness now 4/4: the false-positive/whole-batch-abort defect that capped this at 3/4 is fixed and independently verified across 5 new scenarios (mixed-batch at 3 positions, reverse column omission, empty response), none of which reveal a further correctness gap. Completeness 4/4 and Appropriateness 3/4 unchanged.

reliability.note: Up from 8/12. Fault tolerance and recoverability are now strong: the guard fires correctly regardless of which column is missing or the bad accession's position in a batch, and a batch with one bad accession now finishes with only that one accession skipped -- verified with real, live good-accession downloads in every mixed-batch test. Not full marks: error reporting has a real, reproducible message-accuracy defect (see Input 6) where the guard's message always says 'fastq_ftp not found' even when fastq_md5 is the field actually missing.

performance_context.note: Unchanged from the pre-fix report -- this round's fix is a small, localized guard and did not materially change SKILL.md's length or token cost.

agent_usability.note: Up from 12/16. The false-success failure mode that agent_usability was previously docked for no longer exists; feedback design and error prevention are meaningfully better since the guard reliably fires with an accession-attributed message pointing at the right SKILL.md section. Not full marks: the Common-errors table does not document the message-accuracy quirk found in Input 6 (message names the wrong field in the reverse-omission case).

human_usability.note: Up from 6/8. Forgiveness is substantially improved: across every tested failure shape (missing fastq_ftp, missing fastq_md5, empty response, at any batch position) the script now fails loudly and specifically instead of reporting false success. Not 8/8 because the reverse-omission message names the wrong field, which could send a user chasing the wrong cause even though the safety behavior itself is correct.

security.note: Unchanged. No hardcoded secrets, no eval/exec of raw strings; accession-format validation before interpolation into curl/prefetch is still absent (out of scope for this fix pass).

maintainability.note: Unchanged. This round's fix is a small, localized two-line guard added identically to the SKILL.md inline snippet and download_batch.sh; no new duplication introduced (confirmed by re-reading usage-guide.md against the current SKILL.md, per the fix log's own redundancy check, independently spot-checked).

agent_specific.note: Up from 17/20. Escape Hatches now 4/4: the dbGaP boundary is no longer advisory-text-only -- the shipped code now surfaces the section's own documented recognition signal, verified by direct execution in 5 of this round's 7 inputs. This closes the second P1 from the pre-fix report. Trigger Precision and Composability remain strong.

key_strengths: Both P1s from the pre-fix report are confirmed genuinely fixed by this independent re-audit: the ENA-mirror guard now correctly skips only the bad accession in a mixed batch, verified at all three list positions (first, middle, last) with real live good-accession downloads alongside independently-built synthetic fixtures.

The fix generalizes beyond exactly what the fixer tested: it also correctly catches a reverse-column-omission case (fastq_md5 missing, fastq_ftp present) and a completely empty/malformed ENA response, not just the exact fixture shape the fixer verified.

The dbGaP boundary's own documented recognition signal is now genuinely surfaced by the shipped code (both the inline SKILL.md snippet and download_batch.sh), closing the second P1 (advisory-text-only gap) with a message that names the accession and points directly at the 'Controlled-access (dbGaP) data' section.
No regression: the happy-path single-accession and all-good 3-accession batch flows remain fully correct after the fix, independently re-verified with real accessions and MD5-matched downloads.

No new P0/P1 found across 7 executed inputs; the one new defect (a guard message that misnames which column is actually missing in the reverse-omission case) is cosmetic and does not weaken the guard's safety behavior.

recommendations.title: Guard's error message hardcodes 'fastq_ftp not found' regardless of which column is actually missing
recommendations.problem: When fastq_md5 (not fastq_ftp) is the column genuinely absent from the ENA response, the guard still fires correctly (zero files written, exit 1) but prints 'fastq_ftp not found in ENA response for ${SRR}...', which is factually wrong in this case and could send a user diagnosing the failure toward the wrong field.
recommendations.root_cause: The guard's echo message hardcodes the fastq_ftp field name instead of naming whichever of FTP_COL/MD5_COL was actually found empty.
recommendations.fix: Build the message from which variable is actually empty, e.g. name the missing field(s) explicitly: '[ -z "${FTP_COL}" ] && echo fastq_ftp missing'; '[ -z "${MD5_COL}" ] && echo fastq_md5 missing', combined into one accession-attributed message.
